title: Error Analysis: Finding What Goes Wrong
summary: A score tells you how often the system fails; error analysis tells you why. This lesson covers reading failures systematically, building a failure taxonomy through open coding, ranking categories with a Pareto chart, and slicing metrics to find the groups the average hides.
objectives: Sample and read failures systematically instead of anecdotally
Build a failure taxonomy by open coding, and check that two coders apply it consistently
Rank failure categories with a Pareto analysis and estimate the gain from fixing each
Compute slice metrics with confidence intervals and spot Simpson's-paradox style reversals
Turn findings into a prioritised list of fixes and new eval cases
prerequisites: Pass rates and confidence intervals from [Comparing Systems You Can Trust](/learn/evaluation/comparing-systems), and the confusion-matrix vocabulary from [Success Criteria](/learn/evaluation/success-criteria).
